scope: Guardian loss during connected native production readiness before selection commit

qn90a.coordinator_unchanged_scope: Production readiness fault, automatic rollback/readmission and explicit cleanup

s90d.coordinator_unchanged_scope: Production readiness fault, automatic rollback/readmission and explicit cleanup

qualification: Existing signed package contents were verified against the prior accepted installation inventory before each trial; no production source or package changed.

The unpaused watcher required state-ready selection, a submitted production record, the matching production readiness intent, an active running unit, the expected executable inode/digest and a fresh guardian PID/start-time binding before SIGTERM.
Both original coordinators automatically acquired a distinct held managed executor, verified old process/unit absence and retained state, and committed rollback under the original transaction.
The submitted production record and readiness intent survived rollback for explicit cleanup. Cleanup completed through the service, retired the original handoff units and removed staging and intents.
Original migration requests remain submitted in the journal; separate cleanup requests are completed. Retained jobs, enrollment/configuration, protected files and managed rescue hashes are unchanged.
Each device ended managed-ready and settled on SDK loopback. All three trial/rescue units and all three recorded handoff units are inactive; test witness scopes are absent.
limits: This qualifies one pre-commit production-readiness guardian-loss boundary, not every interruption, post-commit failure, pressure or power-loss case.
The earlier unexplained paused S90D coordinator exit remains unresolved. These trials did not pause or restart the coordinator.
Native-only capability entry, wider lifecycle/pressure/endurance coverage and native-default rollout remain open.
The .NET capability-entry bridge, managed worker fallback and independent rescue remain deployed. No reboot, standby or platform-policy change occurred.
